title: Unheard
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 108
medium: Interactive page (index.html): a blind listening test of two 15-second recordings (a church tower's six bells, CC0; the practice's own synthesised ringing), with the spectrograms the practice judged by revealed only after the listener answers and a playhead running over them; four tries of Plain Bob Minor, each with its picture and the channels that decided its changes; the ringers' blue line drawn from detected blows, mostly refused. A figure (figure.svg); a git-order and record verifier (verify.py).
embodies: How a machine practice perceives a medium it has no sense for. It made change ringing it could not hear, read a real tower's ringing through pictures, numbers and the ringers' own notation one channel at a time, and tagged every change to its bells by the channel that decided it. Pictures decided seven of ten changes, numbers none, belief three. The ringers' notation refused the data, and making its own ringing, whose rows it knew, showed that the refusal judged its instruments, not the tower. The last verdict, whether it sounds like bells, it could not make, and the face hands it to the listener.
project_step: Fifth experiment of the project. Operation: perceiving, the thinnest row (one case, F-166, from The Mould). Takes from The Mould its committed make-render-look-note loop and its finding that the practice's note can outweigh its picture, and from The Draw its tagging of every change by where it came from, now tagged by perception channel (S, N, B, K) instead of by prior or material. Works with and against Cartography, not Tracing (section 4.5: 'Meter is dogmatic, but rhythm is critical', ATP 313; Klee's 'Render visible', ATP 342; T5's refrain) and against Iteration, not Imitation P5 (integration, not imitation; MEOT 195): it imitates a recording on purpose, as the only probe of perception available to a practice without ears, and the face completes rather than replaces by handing the missing sense to the stranger.
material: Helge Klaus Rieder, 'All Saints church, Kirkbymoorside', recorded 2017-07-13, CC0, Wikimedia Commons (MP3 transcode; original 429), 183.4 s; Plain Bob Minor generated from place notation; domain: English change ringing (bells, sound)
seed: synth.py seed 108 in every iterations/iN.json; the A/B order on the face is random per visit and not recorded
